title: Pre-build AC decision is code, not prose
context: Eleven changes shipped without a written promise because the building agent chose the exemption by label.
decision: Code decides: whether anything observable changed is computed from the diff, AC text must read as an outcome (hard validation), the operator is asked only when an existing AC changes or goes away or no single FR owns a new AC, answers come only through a sha256-bound operator channel, the freeze is an append-only record compared with the catalog at finalize, and an unattended ask holds only its own unit.
consequences: No label, tier or keyword logic remains. An agent cannot assert an exemption or answer its own question. The earlier lexical-HOW design replay (15 of 25 cases, 5 false flags) is superseded.
rationale: Operator decision 2026-11-01: everything that code can decide is decided by code; AI only where code cannot decide.
rejected: A lexical HOW test as an ask trigger (false flags); hash-as-freeze (compare with the catalog instead); a wave-wide STRICT-STOP for a question; any label-based exemption
